15:1: We have already discussed the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs. The Almighty’s statement, Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish al-Baqarah 2:17, is a statement about them that they will regret their disbelief and wish that they had been Muslims in this world. Al-Suddi narrated in his interpretation, with his famous chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and other companions, that when the disbelievers of Quraysh were presented to the Fire, they wished that they had been Muslims. It was said that what is meant is that every disbeliever wishes, when he is dying, that he had been a believer. It was said: This is report about the Day of Resurrection, like the Almighty’s saying: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers.’ Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu al-Zura’, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding His statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims, he said: This is about the people of Hell when they see them coming out of the Fire. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Muslim told us, al-Qasim told us, Ibn Abi Farwah al-Abdi told us that Ibn Abbas and Anas ibn Malik interpreted this verse Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims, they interpreted it as the day when God will detain the sinners among the Muslims with the polytheists in the Fire. He said: The polytheists will say to them: What benefit did what you used to worship in this world avail you? He said: So God will become angry on their behalf out of His abundant mercy and bring them out, and that is when He says: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Hammad on the authority of Ibrahim, and on the authority of Khasif on the authority of Mujahid, they said: The people of Hell will say to the monotheists: What did your faith avail you? So when they say that, God says: Bring out whoever has in his heart an atom’s weight of faith. He said: Then His statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, and this is how it was narrated from Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and others. And there are hadiths attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about that. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim At-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Al-Abbas, he is Al-Akhram, told us, Muhammad ibn Mansur At-Tusi told us, Salih ibn Ishaq Al-Jahbadh and Ibn Ulayyah Yahya ibn Musa told us, Maruf ibn Wasil told us, from Yaqub ibn Nabatah, from Abd Al-Rahman Al-Aghar, from Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Some people from the people of La ilaha illa God will enter the Fire because of their sins. Then the people of Al-Lat and Al-Uzza will say to them: What did your saying La ilaha illa God avail you while you are with us in the Fire? Then God will become angry on their behalf and will bring them out and throw them into the River of Life. They will recover from their burning as the moon recovers from its eclipse, and they will enter Paradise and will be called the people of Hell.” A man said: O Anas: Did you hear this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Anas said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire. Yes, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say this. Then Al-Tabarani said: Al-Jahbadh is the only one to narrate it. The second hadith - Al-Tabarani also said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, Abu Al-Shathaa Ali bin Hassan Al-Wasiti told us, Khalid bin Nafi Al-Ash'ari told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Burda, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the people of Hell gather in Hell, and with them whomever God wills of the people of the Qiblah, the disbelievers will say to the Muslims: Were you not Muslims? They will say: Yes. They will say: What benefit did Islam avail you when you became with us in Hell? They will say: We had sins and we were seized for them. So God heard what they said and ordered those who were in Hell from the people of the Qiblah to be taken out. When those who remained of the disbelievers saw that, they said: We wish we were Muslims so we could be taken out as they were taken out." He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: I seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. "Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an. Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims." And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Khalid bin Nafi with it, and he added to it: In the name of God. God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, instead of seeking refuge. The third hadith Al-Tabarani also said: Musa bin Harun told us, Ishaq bin Rahawayh told us, he said: I said to Abu Usama, Abu Rawq told you, and his name is Atiyah bin Al-Harith, Salih bin Abi Tarif told me, he said: I asked Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and I said to him: Did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about this verse, Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims? He said: Yes, I heard him say: God will bring out some of the believers from the Fire after He has taken His vengeance on them. He said: “When God put them in the Fire with the polytheists, the polytheists said to them: ‘You claim that you are the friends of God in this world while He has afflicted you with us in the Fire.’ So when God heard that from them, He permitted intercession for them, so the angels and prophets interceded for them, and the believers interceded until they were brought out by God’s permission. So when the polytheists saw that, they said: ‘If only we were like them, so that intercession could reach us and we could be brought out with them.’ He said: ‘This is the saying of God: ‘Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims.’ So they will be called in Paradise ‘the Jahannamites’ because of the blackness in their faces, and they will say: ‘O Lord, remove this name from us.’ So He will command them to wash themselves in a river in Paradise and that name will be removed from them.’” Abu Usamah acknowledged that and said: Yes. The fourth hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed Al-Narsy told us, Maskeen Abu Fatima told us, Al-Yaman bin Yazid told me on the authority of Muhammad bin Jabr on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali, on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Some of them will be taken by the Fire up to their knees, some of them will be taken up to their waists, and some of them will be taken up to their necks, according to the extent of their sins and deeds. Some of them will remain in it for a month and then be taken out of it, and some of them will remain in it for a year and then be taken out of it. The longest of them will remain in it for the duration of the world from the day it was created until it perishes. Then, when God wants to take them out of it, the Jews, Christians, and those in the Fire from the people of religions and idols will say to those in the Fire from the people of monotheism: You believed in God, His books, and His messengers, so today we and you are in the Fire, equal. So God will become angry with them in a way that He has never been angry with for anything in the past, and He will take them out to a spring in Paradise, which is His saying: ‘Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims.’” His statement, Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, is a severe threat to them and a definite warning, like the statement of God Almighty, Say, ‘Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire.’ And His statement, Eat and enjoy yourselves a little, for you are criminals. That is why He said, And let hope distract them, meaning from repentance and turning back, for they are going to know, meaning the consequences of their actions.

15:4: God Almighty tells us that He did not destroy a city except after the proof had been established against it and its time had come to an end, and that He does not delay a nation whose destruction has come past its appointed time nor does He advance it past its appointed time. This is a warning to the people of Mecca and guidance for them to abandon their polytheism, stubbornness, and atheism, for which they deserve destruction.

Mujahid said in His saying, We do not send down the angels except with the truth," with the message and the punishment, then the Almighty confirmed that He is the One who sent down the message to him, which is the Qur'an, and He is the One who protects it from change and alteration, and some of them are The pronoun in the Almighty’s saying: We will surely protect him refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as in His saying: And God will protect you from the people. The first meaning is more appropriate and is apparent in the context.
15:10: The Almighty says, comforting His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the denial of those who denied him from the infidels of Quraysh 106:He sent before him to the past nations, and that no messenger came to a nation except that they denied him and mocked him. Then He informed that He instilled denial in the hearts of the criminals who were stubborn and arrogant about following the guidance. Anas and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, Thus do We instill it in the hearts of the criminals, meaning polytheism. And His statement, The precedent of the former peoples has already passed, means that He knows what the Almighty did to those who denied His messengers of destruction and devastation, and how God saved the prophets and their followers in this world and the hereafter.

15:14: God the Almighty tells us about the strength of their disbelief, their stubbornness and their defiance of the truth, that if a door was opened for them from the heaven and they started to ascend through it, they would not believe it, but they would say: Our eyes have only been dazzled. Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Ad-Dahhak said: Our eyes have been blocked. Qatadah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Our eyes have been taken. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was made to seem strange to us, but we were bewitched. Al-Kalbi said: Our eyes have been blinded. Ibn Zayd said: Our eyes have been dazzled refers to the drunkard who is not sane.

15:16: The Almighty mentions His creation of the sky in its height and what He adorned it with of fixed and moving planets, for whoever contemplates and repeatedly looks at what he sees of wonders and dazzling signs, his eyes will be confused by it, and with this Mujahid and Qatadah said: The constellations here are the planets. I said: This is like His saying, the Most High, Blessed is He who has placed constellations in the heaven (al-Baqarah 2:17). And among them are those who said: The constellations are the mansions of the sun and the moon. And Atiyyah al-Awfi said: The constellations here are the palaces of the guards. And He made the meteors as guards for them from the rebellious devils so that they would not hear the higher assembly, so whoever rebels and advances to eavesdrop will be approached by a clear meteor and destroy him, so he may have conveyed the word that he heard before the meteor reached him to someone below him, so the other takes it and brings it to his guardian, as it came explicitly in the Sahih. Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as if it were a chain on a rock. Ali said, and others said, “A rock that carries them through it, and when fear is removed from their hearts, they say: What did your Lord say?” They said: To the One who spoke the truth, and He is the Most High, the Great, and the eavesdroppers hear it, and the eavesdroppers are like this, one above the other, and Sufyan described his hand, and he separated the fingers of his right hand, placing them one above the other, so perhaps the meteor reaches the listener before he throws it to his companion and burns him, and perhaps it does not reach him until he throws it to the one next to him, to the one below him, until they throw it to the ground, and perhaps Sufyan said: Until it reaches the ground and is thrown into the mouth of the magician or soothsayer, and he tells a hundred lies with it and he is told the truth, and they say: Did he not tell us on such and such a day such and such would happen, so we found it to be true for the word that was heard from the sky, then the Most High mentioned His creation of the earth and His spreading it out and expanding it and spreading it out, and what He placed in it of firm mountains, valleys, lands and sands, and what He grew in it of crops and proportionate fruits. Ibn Abbas said: From everything is weighed, meaning known. This is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Abu Malik, Mujahid, Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad, Abu Saleh and Qatadah said. Some of them say: It is measured by a measure. Ibn Zayd said: From everything that is weighed and measured by a measure. Ibn Zayd said: What the people of the markets weigh. And His statement: And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, God the Almighty mentions that He has distributed them on the earth in various ways, which is the plural of livelihood. And His statement: And those for whom you are not providers, Mujahid said: They are the beasts and livestock. Ibn Jarir said: They are the male and female slaves, the beasts and livestock. The point is that God the Almighty bestows His favor upon them by making easy for them the means of earning, various means of livelihood, and various ways of livelihood, and by making available to them the beasts that they ride, the livestock that they eat, and the male and female slaves that they use. Their provision is from their Creator, not from them. So they are the ones who benefit, and provision is from God the Almighty.

15:21: The Almighty informs us that He is the Owner of everything and that everything is easy and simple for Him, and that He has the treasures of things of all kinds, And We do not send it down except according to a known measure, as He wills and as He desires, and because of His great wisdom and mercy for His servants in that, not as an obligation, but He has written mercy upon Himself. Yazid bin Abi Ziyad said on the authority of Abu Juhayfah on the authority of Abdullah: There is no year with more rain than another year, but God distributes it among them as He wills, a year here and a year there, then he recited And there is nothing but that with Us are its treasures, the verse, narrated by Ibn Jarir, and he also said: Al-Qasim told us, Hisham told us, Ismail bin Salim told us on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah in His statement, And We do not send it down except according to a known measure, he said: There is no year with more rain than another year or less, but He rains on some people and deprives others of what was in the sea. He said: And it has reached us that with the rain there descend from the angels more than the number of the children of Iblis, and the children of Adam count every drop where It falls and does not grow. Al-Bazzar said: Dawud, he is Ibn Bakir, told us, Hayyan Ibn Aghlab Ibn Tamim told us, my father told me, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The treasures of God are speech. When He intends a thing, He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.” Then he said: Only Aghlab narrates it, and he is not strong. More than one of the early scholars narrated it from him, and only his son narrated it from him. And the Almighty’s statement: And We sent the winds as fertilizers, meaning they fertilize the clouds, so they produce water, and fertilize the trees, so they open their leaves and buds. He mentioned them in the plural form so that they produce, unlike the barren wind, for He made it singular and described it as barren, which is the lack of production, because it only comes from two or more things. Al-A'mash said on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Qais bin Al-Sakn, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, regarding His statement: And We sent the winds as fertilizing agents, he said: The wind is sent and carries water from the sky, then it passes over the clouds until it produces milk as a she-camel produces milk. Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i and Qatadah said the same. Ad-Dahhak said: God sends it upon the clouds and it fertilizes them and they become filled with water. Ubaid bin Umair Al-Laithi said: God sends the bearer of good tidings and the earth stands firm, then God sends the one who excites and stirs the clouds, then God sends the one who reconciles and reconciles the clouds, then God sends the fertilizing agents and they fertilize the trees, then he recited: And We sent the winds as fertilizing agents. Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Abis bin Maimun on the authority of Abu Al-Muhazzam on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The south wind is from Paradise, and it is the one that God mentioned in His Book, and in it are benefits for people. This is a weak chain of transmission. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Yazid bin Ja’diyah Al-Laithi told me that he heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Mukhraq narrating on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created a wind in Paradise after the wind by seven years, and before it is a closed door, and the wind only comes to you from that door, and if it were opened, it would scatter everything between the sky and the earth, and it is the most fragrant wind with God, and it is the south wind among you.” And His statement: And We gave you to drink of it means We sent it down to you sweet, from which you can drink, if We willed, We could make it bitter, as He pointed out in another verse in Surat Al-Waqi'ah, which is the statement of the Most High: Have you seen the water which you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or is it We who send it down? If We willed, We could make it bitter, so why are you not grateful? And in His statement: It is He who sent down water from the sky for you; from it you drink, and from it are vegetation in which you pasture your food. And His statement: And you are not its keepers Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: with what We provide, and it is possible that what is meant is and you are not its guardians, rather We send it down and preserve it for you and make it a source and springs in the earth, and if the Most High had willed, He could have raided it and taken it away, but out of His mercy He sent it down and made it sweet, and preserved it in springs, wells, rivers and other things, so that it would remain for them throughout the year to drink and water their livestock, crops and fruits. And His statement: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death is a statement of the Almighty’s ability to begin creation and to restore it, and that He is the One who gave life to creation from nothingness, then causes them to die, then resurrects them all for the Day of Assembly. And He informed that the Almighty inherits the earth and whoever is on it, and to Him they will return. Then the Almighty informed of His complete knowledge of them, the first of them and the last of them, and He said: And We have certainly known those of you who went before the verse. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The ones who went before are everyone who perished from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, and the ones who came after are those who are alive and will come until the Day of Resurrection. Something similar was narrated from Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ash-Sha’bi and others, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said: There were people who used to stand back in the rows because of women, so God revealed: And We certainly know those of you who go forward, and We certainly know those who lag behind. A very strange hadith was reported in this regard, so Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi told me, Nuh ibn Qays told us, Amr ibn Qays told us, Amr ibn Malik told us, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: There was a beautiful woman praying behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: No, by God, I have never seen anyone like her. Some of the Muslims, when they prayed, would stand forward, meaning so that they would not see her, and some would stand back, so when they prostrated they would look at her from beneath their hands, so God revealed: And We certainly know those of you who go forward, and We certainly know those who lag behind. This is how Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his interpretation, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it in the Book of Interpretation from their Sunans, and Ibn Majah from various chains of transmission on the authority of Nuh ibn Qays al-Hadani, and Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others authenticated him, and it was reported from Ibn Ma’in that he was weak, and Muslim and the people of Sunan transmitted it, and this hadith contains a severe objection, and Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ja’far ibn Sulayman, from Amr ibn Malik, who is al-Nakkari, that he heard Abu al-Jawza’ say in his statement: And We have certainly known those of you who have gone forward in the rows in prayer, those who lag behind. So it appears that it is from the words of Abu al-Jawza’ only, and there is no mention of Ibn Abbas in it. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is more similar to the narration of Nuh ibn Qays, and God knows best. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Yazid bin Ja’diyah Al-Laithi told me that he heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Mukhraq narrating on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created a wind in Paradise after the wind by seven years, and before it is a closed door, and the wind only comes to you from that door, and if it were opened, it would scatter everything between the sky and the earth, and it is the most fragrant wind with God, and it is the south wind among you.” And His statement: And We gave you to drink of it means We sent it down to you sweet, from which you can drink, if We willed, We could make it bitter, as He pointed out in another verse in Surat Al-Waqi'ah, which is the statement of the Most High: Have you seen the water which you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or is it We who send it down? If We willed, We could make it bitter, so why are you not grateful? And in His statement: It is He who sent down water from the sky for you; from it you drink, and from it are vegetation in which you pasture your food. And His statement: And you are not its keepers Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: with what We provide, and it is possible that what is meant is and you are not its guardians, rather We send it down and preserve it for you and make it a source and springs in the earth, and if the Most High had willed, He could have raided it and taken it away, but out of His mercy He sent it down and made it sweet, and preserved it in springs, wells, rivers and other things, so that it would remain for them throughout the year to drink and water their livestock, crops and fruits. And His statement: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death is a statement of the Almighty’s ability to begin creation and to restore it, and that He is the One who gave life to creation from nothingness, then causes them to die, then resurrects them all for the Day of Assembly. And He informed that the Almighty inherits the earth and whoever is on it, and to Him they will return. Then the Almighty informed of His complete knowledge of them, the first of them and the last of them, and He said: And We have certainly known those of you who went before the verse. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The ones who went before are everyone who perished from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, and the ones who came after are those who are alive and will come until the Day of Resurrection. Something similar was narrated from Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ash-Sha’bi and others, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said: There were people who used to stand back in the rows because of women, so God revealed: And We certainly know those of you who go forward, and We certainly know those who lag behind. A very strange hadith was reported in this regard, so Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi told me, Nuh ibn Qays told us, Amr ibn Qays told us, Amr ibn Malik told us, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: There was a beautiful woman praying behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: No, by God, I have never seen anyone like her. Some of the Muslims, when they prayed, would stand forward, meaning so that they would not see her, and some would stand back, so when they prostrated they would look at her from beneath their hands, so God revealed: And We certainly know those of you who go forward, and We certainly know those who lag behind. This is how Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his interpretation, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it in the Book of Interpretation from their Sunans, and Ibn Majah from various chains of transmission on the authority of Nuh ibn Qays al-Hadani, and Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others authenticated him, and it was reported from Ibn Ma’in that he was weak, and Muslim and the people of Sunan transmitted it, and this hadith contains a severe objection, and Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ja’far ibn Sulayman, from Amr ibn Malik, who is al-Nakkari, that he heard Abu al-Jawza’ say in his statement: And We have certainly known those of you who have gone forward in the rows in prayer, those who lag behind. So it appears that it is from the words of Abu al-Jawza’ only, and there is no mention of Ibn Abbas in it. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is more similar to the narration of Nuh ibn Qays, and God knows best. And this is how Ibn Jarir narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Ma’shar, from his father, that he heard Awn ibn Abdullah mention Muhammad ibn Ka’b in his statement: And We have certainly known those of you who have gone forward the dead and the killed, those who lag behind whoever is created after, “And indeed, your Lord will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.” So Awn ibn Abdullah said: May God guide you and reward you. Good.
15:26: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: What is meant by salsal here is dry soil, and it appears that it is like the Almighty's saying: "He created man from clay like that of pottery. And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire." And from Mujahid also, salsal means stinking, and interpreting the verse by the verse is more appropriate. His saying: from black mud means that clay is from black mud, which is clay. And smooth is smooth, as the poet said: Then her waist to the green dome walking on sharpened marble That is, smooth and polished. That is why it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It is wet soil. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak: That the aged mud is the stinking one. And it was said: What is meant by aged here is the poured one. And His statement: And the jinn We created before meaning before man from scorching fire Ibn Abbas said: These are the poisons that kill. And some of them said: The poisons are at night and during the day, and some of them say: The poisons are at night and the heat is during the day. And Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq who said: I entered upon Umar Al-Asamm to visit him, and he said: Shall I not tell you a hadith that I heard from Abdullah bin Masoud, he says: These poisons are a part of seventy parts of the poisons from which the jinn were created, then he recited: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That the jinn were created from the flame of fire, and in another narration: from the best of fire. And on the authority of Amr bin Dinar: from the fire of the sun. And it was narrated in the Sahih: The angels were created from light, and the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you. The purpose of the verse is to draw attention to the honor of Adam, peace be upon him, the goodness of his nature, and the purity of his lineage.

15:28: The Almighty mentions His mention of Adam among His angels before his creation and His honoring him by ordering the angels to prostrate to him, and He mentions the failure of his enemy Iblis to prostrate to him from among the rest of the angels out of envy, disbelief, stubbornness, arrogance, and boasting of falsehood. For this reason, He said: I would never prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay from altered black mud, like His saying: “I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay,” and His saying: Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me? The verse. Ibn Jarir narrated here a strange and amazing trace from the hadith of Shabib bin Bishr on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God created the angels, He said: “Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.” They said: We will not do that, so He sent fire upon them and burned them. Then He created other angels and said to them the same thing, and they said: We will not do that, so He sent Then He sent a fire upon them and burned them. Then He created other angels and said: I am going to create a human being from clay. When I create him, prostrate to him. But they refused. So He sent a fire upon them and burned them. Then He created angels and said: I am going to create a human being from clay. When I create him, prostrate to him. They said: We hear and obey, except for Iblis, who was among the first disbelievers. There is more to be said about this from him. It appears that he was an Israelite, and God knows best.

15:34: God the Almighty mentions that He ordered Iblis with a universal order that he would not disobey or prevent from leaving the position he was in among the highest assembly, and that he is an outcast, meaning he is cast out, and that He followed him with a curse that will continue to be attached to him, following him and repeating it until the Day of Resurrection. And on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he said: When God cursed Iblis, his form changed from that of the angels, and he made a sound, and every sound in the world until the Day of Resurrection is from it, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and that when the wrath that cannot be averted was realized, he asked, out of his complete envy of Adam and his descendants, to look at the Day of Resurrection, which is the Day of Resurrection, and that he was granted that as a lure for him and a respite, but when the sound was realized, God made him ugly.

15:39: God Almighty says, informing about Iblis and his rebellion and insolence, that he said to the Lord: Because You have misled me. Some of them said: He swore by God's misleading him. I said, and it is possible that it was because of what You have misled me and led me astray, I will surely make attractive to them, meaning the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, on the earth, meaning I will make sins attractive to them and make them desire them and incite them to them, and disturb them to them greatly. And I will mislead them all, meaning just as You have misled me and have been able to do that, except for Your chosen servants among them, like His statement: Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few. God Almighty said to him, threatening and warning him, This is a straight path for Me, meaning that all of you will return to Me, so I will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, like His statement, God Almighty: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. It was said: The path of truth returns to God Almighty, and to Him it ends. This was said by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah, like His statement: And upon God is the determination of the way. Qais bin Ubadah, Muhammad bin Sirin, and Qatadah read: This is the path of Ali, straight, like His statement: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise, meaning lofty. The first reading is the most famous. And His statement, Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority, meaning those whom You have decreed guidance for, so you have no way over them or access to them, except for those who follow you of the deviators, is an interrupted exception. Ibn Jarir included here from the hadith of Abdullah bin Mubarak on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhabb, who told us that Yazid bin Qusayt said: The prophets used to have mosques outside their villages, so if the prophet wanted to ask his Lord about something, he would go to his mosque and pray as much as God had decreed for him, then he would ask Him whatever he wanted. While a prophet was in his mosque, the enemy of God - meaning Satan - came and sat between him and the Qiblah, so the Prophet said: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. He said: He repeated that three times, so the enemy of God said: Tell me by what means you will be saved from me? The Prophet said: Rather, tell me by what means you will overcome the son of Adam twice? So each of them took on the other, so the Prophet said: God the Most High says: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority except for those who follow you of the deviators. The enemy of God said: I heard this before you were born. The Prophet said: And God says: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” And by God, I never felt you except that I sought refuge in God from you. The enemy of God said: You have spoken the truth in this, so you will be saved from me. So the Prophet said: Tell me, by what you can overcome the son of Adam? He said: I overcome it when I am angry or in a state of passion. His saying: And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all meaning Hell is the promised place for all who follow Satan, as He said about the Qur’an: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties, the Fire is his promised place Then He informed that Hell has seven gates for each gate a portion is assigned meaning, for each gate a portion of Satan’s followers has been written for them to enter, and they cannot escape from it. May God protect us from it. Everyone enters from a gate according to his deeds, and he settles in a level according to the extent of his deeds. Ismail bin Aliyah and Shu’bah said, both on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Ghanawi on the authority of Hattan bin Abdullah that he said: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib while he was giving a sermon say: Indeed, the gates of Hell are like this - Abu Harun said - layers, one above the other. Israel said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Hubayrah bin Abi Yarim, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The gates of Hell are seven, one above the other, so the first is filled, then the second, then the third, until all of them are filled. Akrima said: Seven gates, seven levels. Ibn Jurayj said: Seven gates: The first of them is Hell, then Laza, then Al-Hutama, then Al-Sa’ir, then Saqar, then Al-Jahim, then Al-Hawiyah. Ad-Dahhak narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. And it was also narrated from Al-A’mash something similar as well. Qatadah said: It has seven gates, for each gate a portion is assigned. By God, they are dwellings according to their deeds. Ibn Jarir narrated them. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: It has seven gates, for each gate a portion is assigned. He said: A gate for the Jews, a gate for the Christians, a gate for the Sabians, a gate for the Magians, a gate for those who associate others with God, who are the disbelievers of the Arabs, a gate for the hypocrites, and a gate for the people of monotheism. So the people of monotheism are to be hoped for, but those are never to be hoped for. Al-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Junaid told us, Uthman ibn Umar told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Hell has seven gates, one of which is for those who draw their swords against my nation - or he said, against the nation of Muhammad. Then he said: We do not know it except from the hadith of Malik ibn Mughul. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abbas ibn al-Waleed al-Khalal told us, Zaid told us - meaning Ibn Yahya - Saeed ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: For each of their gates is a portion allotted, he said: “Among the people of Hell are those whom the Fire will take up to their ankles, and among them are those whom the Fire will take up to their waists, and among them are those whom the Fire will take up to their collarbones. Their dwellings are according to their deeds, and that is what His statement: ‘For each of their gates is a portion allotted.’”

15:51: God Almighty says: And tell them, O Muhammad, about the story of the guest of Abraham, and the guest is used for both the singular and plural like visitation and travel, and how "they entered upon him and said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Indeed, we are afraid of you.'" That is, we are afraid, and he mentioned the reason for his fear of them when he saw that their hands could not reach what he brought to them as hospitality, which was the fat, roasted calf. Then he said, amazed by his old age and the old age of his wife, and fulfilling the promise, "Have you given me good tidings, although old age has touched me? With what do you give me good tidings?" They answered him, confirming what they gave him good tidings of, fulfilling and giving him good tidings after good tidings. "They said, 'We have given you good tidings in truth, so do not be among the despairing.' Some of them read the despairing." So he answered them that he was not despairing, but he was hoping for a child from God, and if he had grown old and his wife had become old, then he knew of God's power and mercy what was more eloquent than that.

However, the waw does not require order, especially if evidence indicates otherwise. So they said to him in response: Did We not forbid you from hosting anyone? In their intoxication, they are wandering blindly. He said: they are hesitating.

15:73: God the Almighty says: Then the blast overtook them which is what came to them from the devastating sound at sunrise, which is its rising, and that was with raising their country to the sky, then turning it upside down and sending stones of baked clay upon them. The discussion of baked clay has been presented in Hud sufficiently. And His statement: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs means that the effects of these apparent punishments on that country are for those who contemplate that and take signs with their eyes and insight, as Mujahid said in His statement: For those who take signs he said: Those who discern. And from Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak: For those who watch. And Qatadah said: For those who consider. And Malik said from some of the people of Madinah For those who take signs for those who contemplate. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arfa told us, Muhammad bin Katheer Al-Abdi told us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the insight of the believer, for he sees with the light of God. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know it except from this source. Ibn Jarir also said: Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told me, al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, al-Furat bin al-Sa’ib told us, Maymun bin Mihran told us on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the intuition of the believer, for the believer sees with the light of God. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Sharhabil al-Himsi told me, Sulayman bin Salamah told us, al-Mu’ammal bin Sa’id bin Yusuf al-Rahbi told us, Abu al-Mu’alla Asad bin Wada’ah al-Ta’i told us, Wahb bin Munabbih told us on the authority of Tawus bin Kaysan on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the intuition of the believer, for he sees with the light of God and with God’s guidance. He also said: Abdul A’la bin Wasil told us, Saeed bin Muhammad Al-Jarmi told us, Abdul Wahid bin Wasil told us, Abu Bishr Al-Muzlaq told us on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas bin Malik who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has servants who know people by their appearance. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it: Sahl bin Bahr told us, Saeed bin Muhammad Al-Jarmi told us, Abu Bishr, whose name is Ibn Al-Muzlaq, said: He was trustworthy, on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has servants who know people by their appearance. And His statement: And it is on a straight path means that the village of Sodom, which was afflicted by what afflicted it of physical and spiritual destruction and stoning, until it became a stinking, foul lake on a path whose paths continue to this day, like His statement: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning * And by night, so will you not reason? And indeed, Jonah is among the messengers. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: And it is on a straight path he said: A landmark. Qatada said: On a clear path. Qatada also said: In one area of the earth. Al-Suddi said: In a clear book, meaning like His statement: And We have recorded everything in a clear register. But the meaning is not as he said here, and God knows best. And His statement: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers, meaning that what We did to the people of Lot of destruction and devastation and Our saving of Lot and his family is a clear and evident proof for the believers in God and His messengers.

15:78: The people of the thicket are the people of Shu'ayb. Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: The thicket is the intertwined trees. Their injustice was in associating partners with God, cutting off the road, and reducing the measure and the weight. So God took revenge on them with the shout, the earthquake, and the punishment of the Day of Shadow. They were close to the people of Lot, after them in time, and equal to them in place. That is why God Almighty said: And indeed, they are on a clear path, meaning a clear path. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and others said: a clear path. That is why when Shu'ayb warned his people, he said in his warning to them: And the people of Lot are not far from you.

15:80: The people of Al-Hijr are Thamud who denied their prophet Salih, peace be upon them. Whoever denies a messenger has denied all the messengers, and that is why they were called deniers of the messengers. God Almighty mentioned that He brought them signs that would prove to them the truth of what Salih brought them, such as the she-camel that God brought out for them by the supplication of Salih from a solid rock. It used to roam their land, drinking for her and they would drink for a specified day. When they rebelled and hamstrung it, He said to them, “Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied.” God Almighty said, As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness to guidance. God Almighty mentioned that they carved out of the mountains, houses, secure. That is, without fear or need for them, but rather out of wickedness, arrogance, and frivolity, as is seen from their actions in their homes in Wadi Al-Hijr, which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by while he was on his way to Tabuk. He covered his head and hastened his mount, and said to his companions, “Do not enter the homes of the punished people unless you are weeping. If you do not…” They wept, and pretended to weep, fearing that what befell them would befall you.” And His statement: The blast overtook them in the morning, meaning the morning of the fourth day, but what they had earned did not avail them, meaning what they had been exploiting from their crops and fruits, the water of which they had withheld from the she-camel until they hamstrung her so that she would not be constrained by the water, so that wealth did not protect them nor did it benefit them when the command of your Lord came.

15:85: God Almighty says: "And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth. And indeed, the Hour is coming" meaning with justice so that He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done the verse, and God Almighty says: "And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire" and God Almighty says: "Did you then think that We created you in vain and that to Us you would not be returned? Exalted is God, the True King. There is no god but He, Lord of the Noble Throne" Then He informed His Prophet of the coming of the Hour and that it would inevitably happen, then He commanded him to forgive the polytheists beautifully for their harm to him and their denial of what he brought them, like His saying: "So pardon them and say, 'Peace.' They are going to know." Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: This was before the fighting, and it is as they said, for this is Meccan and the fighting was only prescribed after the migration. His saying: Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing is a confirmation of the Resurrection and that the Almighty is able to establish the Hour, for He is the Creator who is not incapable of creating anything, the All-Knowing of what was torn apart from the bodies and dispersed throughout the regions of the Earth, like His saying: “Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the All-Knowing. * His command when He intends a thing is only that He says to it, “Be,” and it is. * So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion over all things, and to Him you will be returned.”

15:87: God the Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: As We have given you the Great Qur'an, do not look at the world and its adornments, and the fleeting splendors with which We have given its people to enjoy in order to test them thereby, so do not envy them for what they are in, and do not let your soul be consumed with regrets and sorrow for them for their denial of you and opposition to your religion, And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers meaning be gentle with them, as He says: "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful." There is a difference of opinion about the seven oft-repeated verses, what they are. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak and others said: They are the seven long verses, meaning Al-Baqarah, Al-'Imran, An-Nisa', Al-Ma'idah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, and Yunus. Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr stated this explicitly. Sa'id said: They explain the obligations, limits, stories, and rulings. Ibn 'Abbas said: They explain the parables, report, and lessons. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us: Sufyan said: Al-Mathani: Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Maidah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, Al-Anfal and Bara'ah are one Surah. Ibn Abbas said: No one was given them except the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and Moses was given two of them. Hisham narrated it on the authority of Al-Hajjaj on the authority of Al-Walid bin Al-Aidhar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on his authority. Al-A'mash said on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was given seven long Mathani, and Moses, peace be upon him, was given six. When he threw down the tablets, two were lifted and four remained. Mujahid said: They are the seven long Mathani, and it is said: They are the Great Qur'an. Khasif said on the authority of Ziyad bin Abi Maryam regarding the words of God Almighty: Seven of the Mathani He said: I have given you seven parts: I command, I confirm, I give good tidings, I warn, I give examples, I enumerate blessings, and I inform you of the report of the Qur'an. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim the second opinion that it is Al-Fatihah, which consists of seven verses. This was narrated on the authority of Ali, Umar, Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: The Basmalah is the seventh verse, and God has made it special for you. This is what Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Abdullah Ibn Ubayd Ibn Umair, Ibn Abi Malekah, Shahr Ibn Hawshab, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Mujahid said. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that they are the Opening of the Book and that they are recited twice in every obligatory or voluntary rak`ah. Ibn Jarir chose this and cited as evidence the hadiths that were reported on that, and we have presented them in the virtues of Surat Al-Fatihah at the beginning of the interpretation, and praise be to God. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, mentioned two hadiths here: One of them he said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Ghundar told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Khabib ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Hafs ibn Asim, on the authority of Abu Sa`id ibn al-Mu`alla, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by me while I was praying and called me, but I did not come to him until I had prayed, so I came to him, and he said: What prevented you from coming to me? I said: I was praying, so he said: “Did not God say: ‘O you who believe! Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you.’ Shall I not teach you the greatest Surah in the Qur’an before I leave the mosque?” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to leave, but I remembered, and he said: ‘Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbi Al-‘Alamin’ is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Qur’an which I have been given. The second He said: Adam told us, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, Al-Maqburi told us on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Mother of the Qur’an is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qur’an. So this is a text indicating that Al-Fatihah is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qur’an, but it does not contradict the description of the other seven long verses as such, because of this characteristic in it, just as it does not contradict the description of the Qur’an as being perfect as such, as God the Almighty said: God has sent down the best statement, a Book similar in its parts, similar in its parts. So it is similar in its parts and similar in its parts, and it is also the Great Qur’an, just as when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the mosque that was founded on piety, he pointed to his mosque, and the verse was revealed. In the Quba Mosque, there is no contradiction, because mentioning something does not negate mentioning something else if they share that characteristic, and God knows best. And His statement: Do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, meaning be content with what God has given you of the Noble Qur’an instead of the fleeting enjoyment and pleasures they have. From here, Ibn Uyaynah interpreted the authentic hadith, He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an, to mean that he is content with it instead of everything else, and this is a correct interpretation, but it is not what is meant by the hadith, as mentioned at the beginning of the interpretation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, the companion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hosted a guest and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have anything to fix, so he sent to a Jewish man, “Muhammad, the Messenger of God, says to you: Lend me some flour until the crescent of Rajab.” He said: No, unless I provide proof. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, and he said: By God, I am the most trustworthy of those in heaven and the most trustworthy of those on earth, and if he lends me or sells me, I will repay him. 15:88: God the Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: As We have given you the Great Qur'an, do not look at the world and its adornments, and the fleeting splendors with which We have given its people to enjoy in order to test them thereby, so do not envy them for what they are in, and do not let your soul be consumed with regrets and sorrow for them for their denial of you and opposition to your religion, And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers meaning be gentle with them, as He says: "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful." There is a difference of opinion about the seven oft-repeated verses, what they are. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak and others said: They are the seven long verses, meaning Al-Baqarah, Al-'Imran, An-Nisa', Al-Ma'idah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, and Yunus. Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr stated this explicitly. Sa'id said: They explain the obligations, limits, stories, and rulings. Ibn 'Abbas said: They explain the parables, report, and lessons. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us: Sufyan said: Al-Mathani: Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Maidah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, Al-Anfal and Bara'ah are one Surah. Ibn Abbas said: No one was given them except the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and Moses was given two of them. Hisham narrated it on the authority of Al-Hajjaj on the authority of Al-Walid bin Al-Aidhar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on his authority. Al-A'mash said on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was given seven long Mathani, and Moses, peace be upon him, was given six. Ibn Abbas said: The Basmalah is the seventh verse, and God has made it special for you. This is what Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Abdullah Ibn Ubayd Ibn Umair, Ibn Abi Malekah, Shahr Ibn Hawshab, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Mujahid said. I said: I was praying, so he said: “Did not God say: ‘O you who believe! Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you.’ Shall I not teach you the greatest Surah in the Qur’an before I leave the mosque?” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to leave, but I remembered, and he said: ‘Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbi Al-‘Alamin’ is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Qur’an which I have been given. The second He said: Adam told us, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, Al-Maqburi told us on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Mother of the Qur’an is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qur’an. So it is similar in its parts and similar in its parts, and it is also the Great Qur’an, just as when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the mosque that was founded on piety, he pointed to his mosque, and the verse was revealed. In the Quba Mosque, there is no contradiction, because mentioning something does not negate mentioning something else if they share that characteristic, and God knows best. The clear warner, a warner to the people of a painful punishment that will befall them for denying him, just as it befell the nations that came before them who denied their messengers, and what God sent down upon them of punishment and vengeance. And His saying: the dividers meaning the allies, meaning they allied to oppose the prophets and deny them and harm them, like the saying of the Most High, informing us about the people of Salih, that they said, ‘We will surely kill him and his family by night’ verse, meaning we will kill them at night. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “My example and that with which God has sent me is like that of a man who came to his people and said: ‘O my people, I have seen the army with my own eyes, and I am the naked warner, so escape, escape.’ A group of his people obeyed him, so they set out at night and departed at their leisure and were saved. A group of them denied him and stayed where they were in the morning. Then the army came upon them in the morning, destroyed them and overran them. So that is the example of one who obeyed me and followed what I brought, and the example of one who disobeyed me and denied the truth that I brought.” And His statement: Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts means they divided their revealed books to them, believing in some of them and disbelieving in some of them. Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They have divided the Qur’an into parts he said: They are the People of the Book, they divided it into parts, believing in some of them and disbelieving in some of them. Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: As We sent down to those who divided he said: They believed in some of them and disbelieved in some of them - the Jews and the Christians. Al-Hakam bin Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They made the Qur’an into two parts, meaning magic. Ikrimah said: The biting is magic in the language of the Quraysh, as they say to the sorceress that she is the biter. Mujahid said: His biting parts, they said magic, and they said divination, and they said legends of the ancients. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah gathered with a group of Quraysh, and he was a man of honor among them, and the season had arrived, so he said to them: O people of Quraysh, this season has arrived, and the Arab delegations will come to you in it and they have heard about this companion of yours, so agree on one opinion about it, and do not differ, lest some of you lie to others, and some of your words contradict each other. They said: And you, Abu Abd Shams, speak and establish for us an opinion that we can say. He said: Rather, you speak so that I may listen. They said: We say a soothsayer. He said: He is not a soothsayer. They said: We say a madman. He said: He is not a madman. They said: We say a poet. He said: He is not a poet. They said: We say a magician. He said: He is not a magician. They said: Then what should we say? He said: By God, his words are sweet. You will not say anything about this except that it will be known that it is false. The closest thing to say is that you say he is a magician. So they dispersed from him because of that, and God revealed about them, Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts, categories. By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do, those are the people who said to the Messenger of God. Atiyah Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Omar regarding his statement: We will surely question them all * about what they used to do, he said: about there is no god but God. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri informed us on the authority of Laith, he is Ibn Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: We will surely question them all * About what they used to do, he said: About There is no god but God. Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Sharik Al-Qadi, on the authority of Laith Ibn Abi Salim, on the authority of Bashir Ibn Nahik, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: By your Lord, We will surely question them all, he said: About There is no god but God. Ibn Idris narrated it on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Bashir, on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Ukaim, he said: Al-Tirmidhi and others narrated it on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah, he is Ibn Mas’ud, said: By the One besides Whom there is no god, there is none among you but that God will be alone with him on the Day of Resurrection, just as one of you is alone with the moon on the night of the full moon, and He will say: Son of Adam, what deceived you about Me? Son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? Son of Adam, what did you answer the messengers? Abu Ja`far said on the authority of Ar-Rabi` on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah regarding His statement: {By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do} He said: All the servants will be asked about two things on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:What they used to worship, and what they answered the Messengers. Ibn `Uyaynah said: About your deeds and about your wealth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Al-Hawari told us, Yunus Al-Hadha` told us on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Shaibani on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “O Mu`adh, a person will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about all his efforts, even the kohl on his eyes and the crumbs of clay on his finger. 15:94: God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to convey what He sent him with, to implement it, and to proclaim it, which is to confront the polytheists with it, as Ibn Abbas said in His statement: "So proclaim what you are commanded" meaning carry it out, and in another narration: "Do what you are commanded." Mujahid said: It is reciting the Qur'an aloud in prayer. Abu Ubaidah said on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to hide until "So proclaim what you are commanded" was revealed, so he and his companions went out. And His statement: "And turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We will suffice you against those who mock" means, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and do not pay attention to the polytheists who want to turn you away from the signs of God. "They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise" and do not fear them, for God will suffice you against them and protect you from them, as God the Almighty says: "O Messenger, convey that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people." Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Yahya bin Muhammad bin Al-Sakn told us, Ishaq bin Idris told us, Awn bin Kahams told us on the authority of Yazid bin Dirham, on the authority of Anas, who said: I heard Anas say about this verse, Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers * Who set up with God another god. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by and some of them nudged him, then Gabriel came, I think he said: He nudged them, and it struck their bodies like a stab wound and they died. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The great ones who mocked, as Yazid bin Ruman told me on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, were five men, and they were of advanced age and had honor among their people from Banu Asad bin Abdul Uzza bin Qusayy Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib Abu Zama’ah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as I have been informed, had prayed against him because of the harm and mockery he had received, saying: O God, blind his sight and bereave his children. From Banu Zuhra, Al-Aswad bin Abdul Yaghuth bin Wahb bin Abdul Manaf bin Zuhra, and from Banu Makhzum, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Umar bin Makhzum, and from Banu Sahm bin Amr bin Hisais bin Ka’b bin Lu’ay Al-Aas bin Wa’il bin Hisham bin Sa’id bin Sa’d, and from Khuza’ah, Al-Harith bin At-Talalatah bin Amr bin Al-Harith bin Abd bin Amr bin Malkan. When they persisted in their evil and increased their mockery of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God Almighty revealed: “So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, who set up with God another deity. They are going to know.” Ibn Ishaq said: Yazid bin Ruman told me on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr or another scholar that Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was circumambulating the House. He stood up and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood beside him. Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth passed by him and pointed to his stomach, so he asked for water from his stomach. Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira passed by him and pointed to a wound at the bottom of his heel, which had occurred to him two years before, while he was cutting his garment. He passed by a man from Khuza’ah who was feathering his arrows, and one of his arrows got stuck in his garment and scratched his foot, which was nothing, so he shook it off and killed him. Al-Aas bin Wa’il passed by him and pointed to the sole of his foot, so he went out on his donkey heading to Taif, and it lay down on a thorn and it entered the sole of his foot and killed him. Al-Harith bin At-Talalatah passed by him and pointed to his head, so he blew pus and killed him. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Their leader was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, and he was the one who gathered them. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, similar to the context of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Urwah, in full, except that Saeed says: Al-Harith ibn Ghaytila, and Ikrimah says: Al-Harith ibn Qays. Al-Zuhri said: And he is truthful, he is Al-Harith ibn Qays, and his mother is Ghaytila. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Muqsim, Qatadah, and more than one, that they were five. Al-Sha’bi said: They were seven, and the first is the well-known view: And His statement: Those who set up with God another god - they are going to know is a severe threat and a definite warning to whoever sets up another god with God. And His statement: “And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say. So exalt the praises of your Lord and be among those who prostrate.” That is, We know, O Muhammad, that because of their harm to you, you feel constricted and distressed, but that does not make you weak or prevent you from conveying the message of God. Put your trust in Him, for He is sufficient for you and your supporter against them. So occupy yourself with the remembrance of God, praising Him, glorifying Him, and worshipping Him, which is prayer. For this reason, He said: So exalt the praises of your Lord and be among those who prostrate. As came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Muawiyah ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Katheer ibn Murrah, on the authority of Nu’aym ibn Hammar, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God Almighty said, O son of Adam, do not be unable to perform four rak’ahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you at the end of it. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Makhul, on the authority of Katheer ibn Murrah, in a similar manner. For this reason, whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by something, he would pray. And his saying: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty. Al-Bukhari said: Salim said: Death. This Salim is Salim bin Abdullah bin Omar, as Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Sufyan, Tariq bin Abdul Rahman told me on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty. He said: Death. And this is what Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and others said. The evidence for that is the saying of God Almighty, informing about the people of Hell that they said: We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we engaged in vain talk with those who engaged in vain talk, and we denied the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty. And in the Sahih from the hadith of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit, on the authority of Umm Al-Ala, a woman from the Ansar, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon Uthman bin Maz’un and he had died, Umm Al-Ala said: May God have mercy on you, Abu Al-Sa’ib, for my testimony is that God has honored you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And how do you know that God has honored him? I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, who? He said: As for him, certainty has come to him, and I hope good for him. This noble verse is used as evidence, which is His statement: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty, that worship, such as prayer and the like, is obligatory upon a person as long as his mind is sound, so he prays according to his condition. It was also proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pray standing, and if you are unable to, then sitting, and if you are unable to, then on your side. This is used as evidence to prove the error of those atheists who believe that what is meant by certainty is knowledge. When one of them attains knowledge, he is no longer obligated, according to them. This is disbelief, misguidance, and ignorance, because the prophets, peace be upon them, and their companions were the most knowledgeable of God and the most aware of His rights and attributes, and what He deserves in terms of glorification. They were also the most devout and the most devoted to doing good deeds until death. What is meant by certainty here is death, as we have already mentioned. Praise and thanks be to God, and praise be to God for guidance, and upon Him we must seek help and trust. He is the One who is asked to cause us to die in the most perfect and best of conditions, for He is Generous and Noble. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Hijr, and praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
